title: Ribbon-fan pin resolves the router via a nonexistent node id (8) and asserts against the wrong port capacity (4)
detail: node_slot(8) fails and returns (0, false); the discarded ok makes rs=0, which is only coincidentally the router's slot, so the apex-distance assertion measures the right node by accident. rim uses port_capacity 4 while the router is an 8-port router_mid, weakening the assertion.
recommended_fix: Use `rs, ok := pp.node_slot(&s.topology, 0)` with an expect on ok, and `rim := puck_rim_world(&v, 8)` to match the router_mid under test.

title: Pin suite only exercises the primitive-fallback radii; the shipped sprite-target branches of puck_rim_world/building_foot_world are untested
detail: Every anchor/radius pin runs with sprites disabled, so the sprite-target radius math (the configuration the game and harness actually render with) has no test coverage; only the primitive fallback constants are pinned.
recommended_fix: Add one pin that sets v.sprites.ok=true (stub targets) and asserts puck_rim_world/building_foot_world match the sprite_*_target-derived radii.

title: Dead locals in scan_obstacles: unused `segs` and discarded intersection point `X`
evidence:
app/render/wire_path.odin:448:
	segs := max(1, path.n - 1)
(never referenced again in the proc — the loops use `path.n - 1` directly)

app/render/wire_path.odin:461:
			X, t, ok := seg_cross(a, b, c, d)
(X never used; the parallel edge-scan at line 503 already uses the project's `_` idiom: `_, t, ok := seg_cross(a, b, e[0], e[1])`)
detail: Two dead bindings in the new module; compiles clean (verified with odin check) but inconsistent with the file's own `_` discard idiom and the project's lean-code conventions.
recommended_fix: Delete the `segs` line and change `X, t, ok := seg_cross(...)` to `_, t, ok := seg_cross(...)`.
